title: No coverage of downloadable Agents / capability-package system
reality: v2.3.0 moved Hierarchical Maps, Conversation audio/video calls, and all six table games into optional downloadable packages with package-owned server runtimes; added a full-page Agents → Download Agents library (Writer/Tracker/Misc groupings, Install All/Uninstall All), the Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents catalog repo with a 29-package catalog, and reduced the base Engine by 25,000+ lines, leaving validated capability registries and compatibility bridges. Fresh installs contain no optional agents; existing installs migrate. v2.3.1 added automatic startup upgrade of installed packages from the catalog with rollback; v2.3.2 added capability API 1.3 host services (#3690) and per-mode compatibility badges (#3676); v2.3.3 added compatibility-aware catalog lanes per Engine major (#3712).
fix: Add a 'Downloadable Agents (v2.3)' section to architecture.md describing the Download Agents library, the Marinara-Agents catalog repo, capability API/registries, package-owned runtimes, startup auto-update with rollback, and the fact that fresh installs ship no optional agents; update the big-picture diagram note that packages supply feature code on demand.

title: Agent section still says '22 built-ins ... all disabled by default'
reality: Since v2.3.0 most agents are no longer built-ins: they are downloadable packages (Card Evolution = Writer Agent, Hierarchical Maps = Tracker Agent, etc.) from a canonical 29-package catalog; fresh installs contain no optional agents. Only a few features (e.g. Conversation About Me profile and update_about_me tool) remain built into the Engine (2.3.0).
fix: Rewrite the Agent core-object entry: replace '22 built-ins plus user-defined custom agents' with the v2.3 model — optional agents install from the 29-package Download Agents catalog (Writer/Tracker/Misc), plus user-defined custom agents; note custom agents can run in Conversation, Roleplay, and Game whenever Enable Agents is on (2.3.2 #3692).

title: Storage section describes removed database compatibility stack
reality: v2.3.0 removed the retired database compatibility stack (runtime backend switch, startup migrations, one-time importer and repair readers, old migration scripts, database-file backup handling, external ORM/runtime dependencies). Storage schemas and query expressions are now file-native throughout. STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite and DATABASE_URL-based import no longer exist. v2.3.0 also added enforceable file-native primary/natural-key constraints and fixed shutdown flush draining (#3602); v2.3.2 made native profile imports atomic (#3683).
fix: In Data Storage, delete the 'SQLite is a legacy opt-in (STORAGE_BACKEND=sqlite); DATABASE_URL is only consulted to import old data' sentence and state that as of v2.3.0 storage is file-native throughout with no runtime backend switch or legacy DB importer; optionally note file-native unique-constraint enforcement and atomic profile imports.

title: Game mode missing Tactical Combat preference
reality: v2.3.0 added a Combat Preference to Game mode, chosen in the setup wizard and changeable in Chat Settings → Combat Style: classic narrative combat, or a new tactical grid-RPG battle style on a terrain-painted battlefield with scene-matched backdrops, unit classes, party formations, per-unit movement/attack ranges, counters, crits, misses, and a full enemy phase driven by a deterministic seeded engine at four difficulty levels; animated movement, damage popups, draggable unit inspector/action menu, translucent staged-move previews, restartable encounters, mobile layout. v2.3.3 fixed mobile CYOA choice visibility (#3691).
fix: In the Game Mode section, add a 'Tactical Combat (v2.3)' paragraph covering the setup-wizard Combat Preference, the Chat Settings → Combat Style section, the terrain battlefield, deterministic seeded engine, and the four difficulty levels, distinguishing it from the pre-existing v2.0 'tactical combat UI' wording.

title: Game setup export documented as .txt only
reality: v2.3.2 (#3701) added reusable Game setup exports/imports: Initial Game Setup downloads now produce versioned .marinara-game-setup.json bundles that can refill the New Game wizard, remap available local resources, warn about missing ones, and require a replacement GM connection when necessary.
fix: Update the Session History (v2.2) paragraph in the Game Mode section: the Initial Game Setup export is now a versioned .marinara-game-setup.json bundle that can be re-imported to refill the New Game wizard with resource remapping and missing-resource warnings.

title: Hierarchical Maps not documented at all
reality: Hierarchical Maps exists as a downloadable Tracker Agent package (v2.3.0), enableable in Roleplay and during/after Game creation; its controls live inside its entry in Chat Settings → Agents (v2.3.2 #3679). v2.3.3 made it obey each chat's Enable Agents master toggle across Roleplay/Game UI, prompt generation, retries, tracker patches, carryover, and checkpoints; corrected the v2.3.2 migration that wrongly auto-selected Maps in every chat (#3723); quarantined incompatible Maps 1.0.x runtimes to prevent the 't.select is not a function' crash; and stopped inactive-chat Maps calls that caused the 'Failed to flush 1 game-state patch callback' send-blocking error.
fix: Add Hierarchical Maps to the architecture doc (under downloadable agents and/or Game/Roleplay sections): a downloadable Tracker Agent package for Roleplay and Game, controls nested in Chat Settings → Agents, gated by the Enable Agents master toggle, with the 2.3.3 migration-correction and version-quarantine behavior noted as troubleshooting context.

title: Turn games described as built-in shared engine
reality: v2.3.0 moved UNO, Chess, Poker, 8-Ball Pool, Tic-Tac-Toe, and Rock-Paper-Scissors into optional downloadable packages with package-owned runtimes; fresh installs don't include them. v2.3.2 fixed the six table games to appear in Conversation Commands controls without separate Add Agent entries and made installed games activate their command/runtime contributions without an Engine restart (#3699).
fix: Update the 'Turn games' bullet in Conversation Mode: the six engines are now optional downloadable Conversation-game packages (installed via Download Agents), not base-Engine code; their [command] tokens and slash commands appear once installed, activating without restart. Adjust the /api/turn-games endpoint note to say the games are package-supplied.

title: Conversation Calls rename and Local Whisper ownership
reality: v2.3.2 renamed user-facing 'Conversation Calls' to 'Calls' (package IDs and legacy symbols preserved) (#3676). v2.3.0 made Calls a downloadable package and made Local Whisper a Calls-owned download: Connections shows Local Speech Model controls only while the Calls package is installed, and uninstalling Calls deletes all downloaded Whisper models and the saved selection. v2.3.2 also fixed downloaded Whisper models not being recognized when DATA_DIR was unset (#3671) and fixed the Calls package inventing dialogue on generation failure (package v1.0.4, #3685).
fix: In the Conversation Calls paragraph and the /api/conversation-calls endpoint entry, rename the feature to 'Calls' (noting the legacy 'Conversation Calls' package ID), state it is a downloadable package since v2.3.0, and note Local Whisper models are owned by the Calls package (Connections' Local Speech Model controls appear only while installed; uninstall removes the models).

title: Noodle prompt override description outdated (editable Noodle Prompt)
reality: v2.3.0 added an editable Noodle Prompt at the top of Noodle Settings with a full-screen editor and one-click default restoration; the canonical default now contains the complete adult-platform, persona-authorship, interaction, and JSON instructions, with the separate timeline voice text appended last.
fix: Update the Noodle 'Refresh (generation)' paragraph: the main refresh prompt is now an editable Noodle Prompt (v2.3.0, full-screen editor, restore-default), with the Timeline Voice & Tone text appended last; adjust the 'schema-critical rules stay hardcoded' claim accordingly.

title: Noodle refresh participant selection and token budgets missing
reality: v2.3.2 changed Noodle refreshes to choose active participants before first-time profile generation, skip characters that already have generated profiles, and send only the selected character cards to the timeline model; world/lore context and chat carryover each now have an 8,192-token budget so large invited rosters cannot inflate unrelated generations.
fix: Add to the Noodle Refresh paragraph: participant selection happens before profile generation (already-profiled characters skipped, only selected cards sent), and world/lore context and chat carryover each have an 8,192-token budget (v2.3.2).

title: Noodle persona authorship across switching not documented
reality: v2.3.1 preserved distinct Noodle authorship across persona switching: posts and replies retain their originating persona account and snapshot, timeline prompts identify each persona by handle and stable identity key, and chat carryover summaries name the persona account instead of collapsing activity into the currently selected identity.
fix: In the Noodle Accounts paragraph, add that posts/replies keep their originating persona's account and snapshot when the user switches personas, and carryover summaries attribute activity to the authoring persona (v2.3.1).

title: Noodle Professor Mari exclusion setting missing
reality: v2.3.0 (#3598) added a default-on Noodle setting that excludes Professor Mari from account discovery and future generated activity without deleting existing timeline history.
fix: In the Noodle Accounts paragraph, note the default-on setting excluding Professor Mari from discovery and future generated activity (existing history preserved).

title: Conversation prompt assembly description predates 2.3.1 rework
reality: v2.3.1 reworked Conversation prompt assembly: Peek Prompt groups Conversation turns under 'Chat History'; character join/leave notices become timestamped history events only after the chat has started; reaction syntax lives inside 'Commands'; merged-group speaker-prefix and character-only response boundaries are emitted last in the preset's XML/Markdown/plain format; the built-in Conversation prompt and Marinara preset use identity wording fitting both 1:1 and group chats, with a startup migration for old bundled presets.
fix: Replace/extend the one-line Conversation description in Prompt Assembly with a 'v2.3.1 Conversation assembly rework' note covering Chat History grouping, timestamped join/leave events, reaction syntax under Commands, last-emitted merged-group boundaries, and the preset identity-wording migration.

title: Group Conversation generation model changed to single merged call
reality: v2.3.1 restored Conversation group chats to one merged provider generation per turn — the model chooses every present speaker within the grouped response instead of issuing a separate restricted request for each character (Roleplay Individual mode unchanged). v2.3.2 (#3673) fixed merged group prompts stripping speaker-tag examples.
fix: Update the 'Group DMs are supported' line: Conversation group chats run as a single merged generation per turn where the model picks all speakers (v2.3.1); Roleplay Individual mode remains per-character.

title: Conversation schedule timezone selector missing
reality: v2.3.1 added a global timezone selector to Conversation schedule creation: defaults to the browser-detected IANA timezone, overridable or resettable to the current device zone, syncs across devices, applies to existing and future Conversation chats; schedule generation, presence, autonomous messages, temporal prompt context, and background server polling honor it. v2.3.0 (#3590) fixed blank TZ= handling to inherit the host timezone.
fix: In the Conversation Mode 'Schedules' bullet, add the v2.3.1 global IANA timezone selector (browser-detected default, device-syncing, honored by schedules/presence/autonomous messages/temporal context/polling).

title: Conversation routine-summary ceiling and About Me ownership
reality: v2.3.2 raised Conversation routine-summary generations from a 512-token ceiling to an 8,192-token default, honoring larger Connection overrides and requesting low reasoning effort (#3696). v2.3.2 also moved Conversation About Me drafting from per-editor AI Write controls to Professor Mari; the About Me profile and update_about_me tool remain built into the Engine (2.3.0), not downloadable.
fix: In Conversation Mode (or a summaries note), record the routine-summary 8,192-token default (was 512) and add About Me: drafted via Professor Mari as of v2.3.2, built into the Engine rather than a downloadable agent.

title: Persona fallback claim wrong for Roleplay
reality: v2.3.2 kept new Roleplay chats persona-less when the user selects no Persona — including the first optimistic message snapshot, provider prompt, scene generation, and combat context; only Conversation mode may fall back to the globally active Persona. architecture.md's Persona section says unconditionally 'the active persona is substituted for {{user}} macros in prompts.'
fix: Amend the Persona core-object entry: the active persona substitutes {{user}} when a persona is selected; persona-less Roleplay chats stay persona-less end-to-end, and only Conversation mode falls back to the globally active Persona (v2.3.2).

title: Roleplay summary truncation limits removed
reality: v2.3.2 removed Roleplay Summary's 2,000-character per-source-message truncation and the 64 KiB compiled-summary ceiling in chats.json, so chapter-length messages and accumulated summaries remain complete unless the model rejects the request.
fix: Append to the Chat Summary (v2.2) paragraph: as of v2.3.2 there is no per-message 2,000-char truncation or 64 KiB compiled-summary cap; summaries are bounded only by the model/connection.

title: New env vars CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED missing
reality: v2.3.3 (#3730) added CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS for slow Conversation, Roleplay, and Game providers, and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false for persistent launcher update opt-out on Windows, macOS/Linux, and Termux without disabling manual updates.
fix: Add both env vars to the doc's env/config coverage (near the VIDEO_GEN_TIMEOUT_MS troubleshooting list or a general env-var note): CHAT_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS (chat-generation timeout for slow providers) and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED=false (launcher auto-update opt-out, manual updates unaffected).

title: Bot Browser renamed to Card Browser / Download Cards
reality: v2.3.0 renamed Bot Browser to Card Browser throughout the interface, docs, onboarding, and Professor Mari guidance, renamed 'Browse Online' to 'Download Cards', and unified it with the library shell as 'Cards Library'. architecture.md still says characters can be 'browsed from Chub.ai via the Bot Browser' and lists '/api/bot-browser/*'.
fix: Rename 'Bot Browser' to 'Card Browser' (aka Cards Library / Download Cards) in the Character section; keep the /api/bot-browser/* route path but note the user-facing name changed in v2.3.0.

title: Venice.ai missing from image-generation providers
reality: v2.3.2 (#3682) added Venice.ai as an Image Generation service with authenticated live image-model discovery and native /image/generate support, model-aware sizing, and validated base64 responses. v2.3.3 also added persistent NovelAI V4.5 style plates with independent strength/fidelity and subject-count framing (#3725, #3726).
fix: Add Venice.ai to the 'Image gen:' provider list in Providers Supported; optionally note the NovelAI V4.5 style-plate support.

title: What's New window and generation-completion notifications missing
reality: v2.3.0 added a one-time, version-aware What's New window (post-onboarding, Professor Mari-hosted, links to the GitHub release, remembers the shown version), and separate opt-in browser/Android generation-completion notifications for manually started Conversation, Roleplay, Visual Novel, and Game replies that finish while Marinara is unfocused (#3588), without changing autonomous-message notification preferences.
fix: Add both to Special Features Worth Knowing: the version-aware What's New window (v2.3) and the opt-in generation-completion notifications for unfocused sessions (v2.3, #3588).

title: Defaults category 'Illustrator' renamed 'Images'
reality: v2.3.0 renamed the Connections 'Illustrator' defaults category to 'Images' and consolidated selfie configuration as 'Illustrator Settings' inside Chat Settings → Agents; image/video settings and /illustrate & /selfie commands are hidden until the Illustrator package is installed.
fix: Update the Connection Defaults categories to 'Main, Agents, Images, Videos' and note that Illustrator is now a downloadable package gating /illustrate, /selfie, and Gallery generation controls (v2.3.0).

title: 'No plugin marketplace' claim now misleading
reality: Since v2.3.0 Marinara has an official Download Agents catalog (Pasta-Devs/Marinara-Agents) for installing/updating/uninstalling verified first-party capability packages, with startup auto-update (2.3.1) and per-Engine-major catalog lanes (2.3.3 #3712). Client-side CSS/JS extensions remain manual installs, but the blanket 'No plugin marketplace' bullet in What's NOT Built-In now overstates the limitation.
fix: Revise the 'No plugin marketplace' bullet: official first-party agent packages install from the built-in Download Agents catalog (v2.3); there is still no third-party marketplace, and CSS/JS extensions remain manual installs.

title: Spotify DJ / Music DJ is now a downloadable agent
reality: v2.3.0 replaced stale music player controls with 'Download Music DJ Agent to configure' guidance whenever the Music Player toggle is on without Music DJ installed; Music DJ is one of the optional downloadable packages, and Game setup only shows Music DJ, Lorebook Keeper, Illustrator, and Hierarchical Maps controls when their packages are installed.
fix: Update the Spotify integration bullet: the Music DJ agent is a downloadable package (v2.3); the always-available Music Player toggle prompts users to download it when missing.
